text: Harness-Bench (2026 preprint): among configurable harnesses, the top scorer led the lowest by about 24 points on the same tasks and model-backend pool; the authors conclude that agent performance should be reported at the model-harness level, not attributed to the base model alone. (secondary summary of arXiv 2605.27922 from a web search, 2026-10-14)

Arena.ai harness tax post: across 21 model-harness pairs on SWE-bench Lite and Terminal-Bench 2.0, harness choice has little effect on task success rate, but can significantly affect the cost. (secondary summary from a web search, 2026-10-14)

davila7/claude-code-templates is reported at 25.6K GitHub stars and 2.6K forks, and its templates include complete project configurations with CLAUDE.md, .claude files and .mcp.json. (third-party aggregator page via web search, not checked on GitHub, 2026-10-14)

Awesome Claude Code is a curated collection of slash commands, CLAUDE.md files, CLI tools and workflows, listed at about 21.6k GitHub stars as of a January 23, 2026 update. (ClaudeLog listing via web search, not checked on GitHub, 2026-10-14)

Existing community tools already audit Claude Code configuration: claude-md-optimizer, claudemd-optimizer, claudit, token-optimizer and claudelint; token-optimizer audits CLAUDE.md, MEMORY.md, skills, MCP servers, commands and settings and reports dollar savings estimates. (web search result summaries, install steps and licenses not checked, 2026-10-14)

Soul Spec by ClawSouls offers a community registry with one-command install for sharing agent personas, while plain CLAUDE.md sharing is described as manual copy-paste. (third-party page via web search, 2026-10-14)

ETH Zurich paper 'Evaluating AGENTS.md' (arXiv 2602.11988, v1 2026-02-12, v3 2026-09-29): 'providing context files does not generally improve task success rates' while 'increasing inference cost by over 20% on average'; this holds across LLMs, coding agents, and both LLM-generated and developer-committed context files. (abstract read directly on arxiv.org/abs/2602.11988, 2026-10-14)

A third-party benchmark (Systima, cited by Kunal Ganglani's blog) found Claude Code's baseline before the first prompt is about 33,000 tokens versus about 7,000 for OpenCode, and a 72KB AGENTS.md added about 20,000 tokens. (secondary blog summary of a third-party benchmark, not checked at the source, 2026-10-14)

Community reports summarized in a 2026 MCP token autopsy say a session with 5-10 MCP servers typically starts with 50,000-67,000 tokens of overhead, and one user reportedly cut MCP overhead from 51K to 8.5K tokens with the ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH setting. (secondary blog summaries of community reports, 2026-10-14)

token-optimizer (alexgreensh/token-optimizer) states a target of 5-15% context recovery through config cleanup, up to 25%+ with autocompact management, and audits CLAUDE.md, MEMORY.md, skills, MCP servers, commands and settings. (catalog listings via web search, not checked on GitHub, 2026-10-14)
A documented case cut an always-loaded 1,358-line file to 807 lines and reduced overhead by 41%. (secondary blog summary, 2026-10-14)

ETH Zurich paper arXiv 2602.11988 v3 body (HTML read 2026-10-14): LLM-generated context files changed success by -0.5 points on SWE-bench and -2 points on CTXbench (neither significant) and raised cost by 20% and 23%; developer-written files raised success by 2.4% (p = 21%, not significant); for Sonnet-4.5 on CTXbench success was 73.2% with no file, 65.2% with an LLM-generated file and 70.3% with a developer file; the authors write 'We therefore suggest omitting LLM-generated context files for the time being.'
